<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par54" />9:6, 16:10.—Like the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּקַטַּ֫לְנָה}} ({{GHGpar|52|n}}), forms occur in {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} like {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְהַלַּ֫כְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=6|verse=7}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=13}}, and so in ''Hithpoʿēl'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=13}}; with ''ē'' only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=1}}.—In the Aramaic manner an {{GHGterm|infinitive Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַבְּרוּת}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=23}} (cf. the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} inf. {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁמָעוּת}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=26}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|l}}
2. As instances of the {{GHGterm|reflexive}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקַטֵּל}} (connected with {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}) a few reflexive forms of the verb {{GHGheb|text=פָּקַד}} (''to examine'') are also probably to be reckoned. Instead of a {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in a sharpened syllable after the first radical, these take {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} in an open syllable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפָּֽקְדוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=15.17}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִתְפָּקֵד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=9|hidebook=1}}. The corresponding passive form {{GHGheb|text=הָתְפָּֽקְדוּ}} also occurs four times, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=1|verse=47}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=2|verse=33|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=26|verse=62|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=27}}. According to others, these forms are rather reflexives of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, in the sense of ''to present oneself for review, to be reviewed'', like the Aramaic ''ʾIthpeʿēl'' (Western Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=אִתְקְטֵל}}, Syr. {{GHGheb|text=אֶתְקְטֵל}}) and the Ethiopic ''taqat<sup>e</sup>la'', Arab. ''ʾiqtatala'', the last with the ''t'' always placed after the first radical (cf. above, b); but they are more correctly explained, with König, as {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} forms, the doubling of the {{GHGheb|text=ק}} being abnormally omitted.—Such a reflexive of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, with the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} transposed, occurs in {{GHGheb|text=הלתחם}} (on the analogy of O.T. Hebrew to be pronounced {{GHGheb|text=הִלְתַּחֵם}}) in the inscription of the Moabite king ''Mêšaʿ'', with the meaning of the O.T. {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִלְחַם|translate=to fight, to wage war}}: see the inscription, lines 11, 15, 19, and 32; in the first two places in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶלְתַּחֵם}}; in line 19 in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} with suffix, {{GHGheb|text=בְּהִלְתַּֽחֲמֹה בִי|translate=in his fighting against me}}.
<section end="par54" />
<section begin="par55" />{{GHGpar-heading|55|Less Common Conjugations}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|a}}
Of the less common conjugations ({{GHGpar|39|g}}) some may be classed with {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, others with {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}. To the former belong those which arise from the lengthening of the vowel or the repetition of one or even two radicals, in fact, from an internal modification or development of the stem; to the latter belong those which are formed by prefixing a consonant, like the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}. Amongst the conjugations analogous to {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} are included the {{GHGterm|passive}} forms distinguished by their vowels, as well as the reflexives with the prefix {{GHGheb|text=הִתְ}}, on the analogy of {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|55|b}}
The following conjugations are related to {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, as regards their inflexion and partly in their meaning:

1. {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=קוֹטֵל}}, passive ''Pôʿal'' {{GHGheb|text=קוֹטַל}}, reflexive ''Hithpôʿēl'' {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקוֹטֵל}}, corresponding to the Arabic conj. iii. ''qâtălă'', pass. ''qûtĭlă'', and conj. vi. reflexive ''tăqâtălă''; {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יְקוֹטֵל}}, {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מְקוֹטֵל}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect passive}} {{GHGheb|text=יְקוֹטַל}} &c. Hence it appears that in Hebrew the ''ô'' of the first syllable is in all the forms obscured from ''â'', while the passive form is distinguished simply by the ''a''-sound in the second syllable. In the strong verb these conjugations are rather rare. Examples: {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מְשֹֽׁפְטִי|translate=mine adversary, who would contend with me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=טְלֽוֹשְׁנִי}} (denominative from {{GHGheb|text=לָשׁוֹן|translate=the tongue}}) ''slandering'' (as if ''intent on injuring with the tongue'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=101|verse=5}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} (The ''Q<sup>e</sup>ré'' requires {{GHGheb|text=מְלָשְׁנִי}} ''m<sup>e</sup>lŏšnî'' as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וּגְדָול־}}); {{GHGheb|text=זֽׄרְמוּ|translate=they have poured out}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=18}} (if not rather {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}); {{GHGheb|text=יוֹדַ֫עְתִּי|translate=I have appointed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=3}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=הוֹדַ֫עְתִּי}} should be read); {{GHGheb|text=יְסֹעֵר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=13|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁרֵשׁ|translate=to take root}}, passive<section end="par55" /><noinclude>
